items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: But I played a picnic at the lake with a mandolin, with a band, a whole band, with Joe Oliver's band.

ctx.x: What about cakewalks? Did you ever play any cakewalks? I played quadrille, cakewalks.

Yeah. Yeah. You know, I'll tell you the truth. You might take... But I don't know if it's ever in the party. No, it's all day, all gone. But I played a picnic at the lake with a mandolin, with a band, a whole band, with Joe Oliver's band. They didn't have no violin, they didn't put me on the mandolin. I was leading, I was leading the band with mandolin. I knew all them numbers. Yeah. That's the truth. You never heard of them. You had a seven-piece band, and I was leading with a mandolin. Now you know, a mandolin…
Did you ever know two guys, they called themselves Jack and Jill? Uh... Jack Dowden, he played mandolin. And Jules Batiste, he played guitar?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: 1912 Liberty near Iberville, Huntson Nagel's Dance Hall with Joe Oliver's Band.

ctx.x: I'll ask a couple questions, see like where you were born right here in New Orleans.

I started the playing in 1904 at Hugh Cloth's Dance Hall with O'Neill Lavish's Band, Franklin Y. Iberville. 1905 at Tom Anderson with Moran's Band, Basin and Iberville. 1907 at Harry Parker's Dance Hall, Dawson and Minetta's Band, Franklin between Iberville and Benwood. 1910 at Biller Phillips Dance Hall, Cornelius Jackson's Band, Franklin near Iberville. 1912 Liberty near Iberville, Huntson Nagel's Dance Hall with Joe Oliver's Band. 1915 with Chris Kelly's Band. 1918 Kid René's Band. 1921 Pippa Light Charles Band.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: Yeah, I played violin with him, you know. I didn't stay with him long.

ctx.x: No, no. Oh, that was the Pelican, like, was on Rampard and Gravia. That was, that had a stairs that go up. Balcony in front. Yeah. That's where we, uh, me and Kid Rene was playing it. We played there. I played there with Rene at the Pelican. On Rampard between, uh, Neb Gravia. Yes, I know by Neb Gravia. Well, we had, well, Beansy was running that place. But they had a front porch down on the gallery, you see? And we used to go out and play a couple of numbers out on that front gallery before we'd go in and play,…
Yeah. Well, I was gonna ask again, that Oliver band with Joe Oliver, who else was in that? Can you remember, who else played with him in those days when you were working with him?
Well, he had, uh, he had Chris Minor playing the drum. Chris Minor was on the drum. And he had, uh, George Foster, Pop Foster on the bass. And I played guitar.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1962-01-31
items.q: And him and Joe Oliver formed a band with Chicago. And they worked together with two of them in the same band until they fell out.

ctx.x: Well, uh, they'd have six pieces. We went to the Junk Hotel and played there. Well, he had Son Thomas playing guitar. I was playing bass. He had, uh, Dominic Remy on the trumpet. They had two trumpets. He had T-Boy Remy with him. And he had a fella called Pill on the clarinet. He died. He had a little bow-legged fella called Pill. Well, after that, well, Louis played around spot jobs around different places. And then, that's when he went up the line. Joe Oliver got with Joe Oliver. And him and Joe Oliver formed a…
And, uh, did he have a trombone down here, Louis? Used the trombone much?
